I got a similar error building Android custom templates of the official 4.6.3 (build host is Windows 11 x86_64):

```
[ 80%] Linking Shared Library bin\libgodot.android.template_release.x86_64.so ...
[100%] ERROR: ld.lld: error: ld-temp.o <inline asm>:1:7: invalid operand for instruction
        divq $-4611686018427387904
             ^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
```

There were no errors when I was building the templates (with the same flags) from the 4.6.2 sources a few months back. I'll try to downgrade Android NDK back to 28.2.13676358 (4.6.3 uses 29.0.14206865), change `config.gradle` accordingly, and build again. If it changes anything, I'll post a short follow-up.
I'm afraid a workaround mentioned above (switching to gcc) is a no-go here, as the Android toolchain is now LLVM-based (AFAIK).

As far as I know, the problem is in LLVM's LTO. This exact instruction is being emitted on full LTO (`-flto=full` clang option). GCC uses a different LTO mechanism, therefore they do not experience such bug. Try to use thin LTO, or turn it off as a temporary workaround, if you want to use LLVM.

I am not sure whether it is a Godot bug or a compiler bug, so I don't expect to see it fixed soon, as it is a linker step error and is extremely hard to investigate.

I remember being able to compile Godot with full LTO using a lower llvm toolchains version. You may also try to downgrade android ndk, keeping full LTO on.

You're probably right, I've got `lto=full` in build flags. I'm currently building with NDK 28 (but it takes a while). If it doesn't help, I'll swith to thin LTO or turn it off completely. BTW, is LLVM's `-flto=thin` directly mapped to `lto=thin` in Godot build flags?

> You're probably right, I've got `lto=full` in build flags. I'm currently building with NDK 28 (but it takes a while). If it doesn't help, I'll swith to thin LTO or turn it off completely. BTW, is LLVM's `-flto=thin` directly mapped to `lto=thin` in Godot build flags?

I'm pretty sure it is. To toggle LTO you can use `lto=thin` or `lto=none` instead, there is no need to use cflags for that. But if you do, you better remove -flto from cflags.
With NDK 28.2.13676358 the error persists (in Godot 4.6.3 - there was no error in 4.6.2). Switching to NDK 29 and thin LTO.
Thin LTO worked fine with 4.6.3 and NDK 29.0.14206865. Thanks for the suggestions.
